text.p: These are the leading stories in this morning's French newspapers.

LIBERATION - GEC Alsthom would draw on Framatome funds to finance a bid for the energy division of Westinghouse, according to a GEC Alsthom document. The newspaper said talks on the acquisition concluded on July 25.
LES ECHOS - Financial markets concerned about possible rate increases by the Fed, Bundesbank, as dollar hits eight-year high against mark, franc.
- GEC Alsthom acquires three plants in New York state.
- Insurer AGF pursues asset sales, sheds 850 million franc property portfolio to MAAF.
- Cie Bancaire sells 4.7 billion francs of UCB Bank property assets to Birmingham Mildshires Building Society.
TRIBUNE - Dollar's rise worries bourse, markets fear a Bundesbank reaction.
- French carmakers Renault and PSA Peugeot Citroen sell cars at higher prices in France, according to a European Commission study of car prices.
- Seventy percent of large retailers say July sales were equal to or higher than last July, according to IFLS association.
- Rhone-Poulenc may end up paying more for Rhone-Poulenc Rorer than envisaged. Bourse awaiting terms of deal.
AGEFI - Degremont climbs on speculation of buyout by parent Suez Lyonnaise des Eaux.
FIGARO - Rate of burglary of primary residence falls, according to insurance sources.

INTERNATIONAL HERALD TRIBUNE - Pressure on Deutschemark underscores uncertainty over how Europe would respond to eventual instability in its new single currency; Paris and Bonn differ over political control of the future European Central Bank.
